http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27933.text: Big News Network.com Polish MP calls for migrant crackdown after Ukrainian kills priest A Ukrainian who had entered Poland from Germany carried out a stabbing attack last week Poland should tighten its border controls following a deadly knife attack by a Ukrainian national, former Polish Deputy Prime Minister and current Law and Justice (PiS) MP Henryk Kowalczyk has said, warning that the killing could fuel another wave of anti-Ukrainian sentiment. A 31-year-old Ukrainian citizen attacked five people at a Catholic abbey in the southeastern city of Jaroslaw on Thursday, killing a priest and injuring four others, according to Polish officials. The suspect, who according to investigators had entered Poland from Germany overnight and was apparently heading toward the Ukrainian border, was detained at the scene. Prosecutors are investigating the circumstances and motive behind the attack. "This will certainly trigger another wave of hostility toward Ukrainians," Henryk Kowalczyk, an MP with the conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, told Polish Radio's Jedynka on Friday. The lawmaker stressed that politicians should not inflame anti-Ukrainian sentiment, but added: "We are talking about the facts. People draw their own conclusions: a Ukrainian killed a Polish priest and injured many people. There is no need to fuel anything here." Kowalczyk argued that the incident should prompt Warsaw to step up border controls, reiterating that the suspect had entered Poland from Germany. "We do not control the German-Polish border at all," he said, contrasting Warsaw's approach with Berlin's selective checks. Poland "cannot accept all migrants who ended up in Germany and then enter our country," he argued. The MP also said that punishing the attacker was not enough, urging the Polish authorities to draw broader conclusions from the deadly incident. "This is a signal that we should check people in advance, rather than just say that we will punish them severely," he said. The attack comes as Polish attitudes toward Ukrainian migrants have deteriorated sharply. A July survey by polling agency CBOS found that, for the first time since it began tracking the issue, a majority of Poles opposed accepting them, with 52% against and 42% in favor. Support had stood at 94% shortly after the escalation of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022. Another CBOS poll published in September found that the share of Poles who believe reconciliation with Ukrainians is possible had fallen to a record low of 53%, while 38% said it was impossible. Kiev's ambassador to Warsaw, Vasily Bondar, said earlier this week that attacks and acts of aggression against Ukrainians had risen by around 30% in the first half of 2026, as public attitudes toward refugees continued to sour. He said Polish police had recorded 180 such incidents during the period, compared with 275 throughout 2025. Relations between Warsaw and Kiev have also been strained by historical grievances. Tensions escalated after Ukraine's Vladimir Zelensky named a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which Poland holds responsible for massacres of Polish civilians during World War II. Polish President Karol Nawrocki subsequently stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle, Poland's highest state honor, citing the decision to honor the UPA. Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/AP Trump administration Trump ‘border czar’ says Ilhan Omar could be ‘of course’ denaturalized and deported Officials allege congresswoman, whose home was raided by federal agents, or family violated law to obtain citizenship José Olivares in New York Sun 18 Oct 2026 18.16 BST Last modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 18.17 BST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Tom Homan , Donald Trump’s “border czar”, has said that the Republican presidential administration could “of course” strip Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar of her citizenship and deport her. Homan’s comments during a Saturday appearance on Fox News were the first remarks explicitly mentioning denaturalization and deportation in connection with Omar that were attributed by name to a top Trump administration official since federal agents raided the Minnesota US House representative’s home on 12 October. The search of Omar’s home sparked major backlash and accusations that the Trump administration was weaponizing the federal government to target a political rival whom the president and his supporters have openly fantasized about denaturalizing and deporting . Ilhan Omar’s attorneys say federal search of her home was ‘neither justified nor lawful’ Read more The federal government’s investigation into the most prominent Somali American in the US is to see whether Omar or her family violated any laws when obtaining her citizenship. The investigation was launched only weeks before the November midterm elections , in which Omar is on the ballot. When asked on Saturday by a Fox News host whether the investigation into Omar could involve “denaturalizing and then deporting her”, Homan answered: “Of course”. “If you lie during the naturalization process, there is a process to denaturalize somebody,” Homan said. “We’ve done it before. It’s a long, tedious process, but it’s been done before. “And certainly, if the evidence points that way, that could happen.” Homan also seemed to imply during his Fox News appearance that the federal government is investigating Omar for other allegations – but refused to give details. “I’m not going to go there,” Homan said. “I know things, but that’s a question for the FBI.” Omar – a naturalized US citizen from Somalia – was a child when her father filled out the immigration paperwork which the federal government is evidently scrutinizing. Her father, Nur Omar Mohamed, died in June 2020. View image in fullscreen Tom Homan applauds as Donald Trump speaks at a rally in Syracuse, New York, on 9 October. Photograph: Mandel Ngan/AFP/Getty Images In a letter after her home was searched, Omar’s attorneys accused the US justice department of potentially influencing an election in violation of longstanding internal policy. The move to investigate Omar came amid a heightened offensive by the administration in pursuit of its aggressive anti-immigrant crackdown. In addition to funneling resources and deploying droves of officials to arrest, detain and deport undocumented immigrants throughout the country, the administration has also escalated its on offensive on legal migration . The administration has been pursuing dozens of cases nationwide in which they are attempting to denaturalize Americans born outside of the US, who they claim fraudulently obtained their citizenship. As Homan alluded to on Sunday, the lengthy denaturalization process requires a federal investigation and drawn-out court proceedings. Nonetheless, as of April, the US justice department had reportedly identified nearly 400 foreign-born citizens that it sought to investigate. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion The investigation into Omar follows unsubstantiated accusations by rightwing figures who support Trump that she obtained her citizenship fraudulently. Omar denies the accusations, which also include allegations that her ex-husband is her brother, whom she only married so he could obtain immigration status in the US. Ilhan Omar’s phone seized and relatives subpoenaed in criminal inquiry, source says Read more The federal government reportedly seized Omar’s phone during the raid on her home and has issued more than a dozen subpoenas, including of Omar’s relatives. Omar’s attorneys have demanded that the federal government return her property and preserve any audio or video taken during the search. Omar has said she and her family fled Somalia’s civil war when she was eight and spent years in a refugee camp in Kenya. She and her family came to the US in the 1990s, and she became a naturalized US citizen in 2000, according to her lawyers. There is “no legitimate basis for any suggestion that she has violated any law concerning her citizenship status”, said her attorneys’ letter, which was first reported by the Wall Street Journal . After the raid on her home, Omar posted on X that she was “ok”. “Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” Omar also wrote. She said: “Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns” for years – and “this is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.” “I will not be silenced,” Omar added.
